subject.title: fix(infra): make exec-approvals lock ownership filesystem-safe

question: Which open implementation should be the canonical fix for the exec-approvals VirtioFS lock leak: this rebased branch or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028?
rationale: Both PRs target the same security-sensitive authorization-store failure and share the same proposed design; choosing one determines whose exact head must receive final runtime proof and CI repair.

options.title: Adopt one canonical PR after proof refresh
options.body: Choose the branch with the clearest current-head VirtioFS proof and clean checks, and close the other only after the selected PR is viable.

options.title: Prefer the original implementation
options.body: Continue review on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028 because it contains the original detailed live-redeployment evidence, then transfer any verified improvements from this rebase deliberately.

options.title: Pause both for a narrower owner-led rewrite
options.body: Pause both branches if the shared-lock and reentrancy contract needs a design review beyond a focused bug repair.

recommendation.title: Adopt one canonical PR after proof refresh
recommendation.body: Choose the branch with the clearest current-head VirtioFS proof and clean checks, and close the other only after the selected PR is viable.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the original production reproduction and authored the overlapping async-lock implementation.
